summary: Strong bullish reversal day. After a brutal -2.1% selloff on Jan 20 triggered by Trump's Greenland tariff threats against 8 European nations, the setup for Jan 21 is a classic relief rally. Trump speaks at Davos WEF at ~1pm ET and by ~2:30pm ET announces he's reached a 'framework deal' with NATO's Rutte on Greenland, pausing all threatened tariffs on European nations. Markets were 'still sinking' in the morning on tariff fears, then staged a massive afternoon reversal. The Dow closed +588pts (+1.2%), S&P 500 +1.16% to 6,875.62, Nasdaq +1.18%. This is a textbook 'buy the dip after geopolitical scare' setup, amplified by oversold conditions from the prior day's sharp decline.

sections.title: Geopolitics
sections.content: DOMINANT CATALYST: Trump announced Jan 17 that 8 European nations (Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, UK) face 10% tariffs Feb 1 (escalating to 25% June 1) unless Greenland is sold. This triggered the Jan 20 selloff (-2.1% on S&P). On Jan 21 at Davos, Trump first said he 'won't use force' for Greenland, then at ~2:30pm ET posted he reached a 'framework deal' with NATO Secretary General Rutte, pausing all European tariffs. Markets surged on relief. Greenland crisis Wikipedia shows Denmark committed $13.7B to Arctic defense. Separately, the Supreme Court IEEPA tariff challenge was pending (ruled Feb 20 that IEEPA tariffs unconstitutional 6-3). Ken Griffin at Davos warned trade policy uncertainty is weighing on global investment decisions.

sections.title: Macro
sections.content: Fed funds rate at 3.50-3.75% after three consecutive 25bp cuts. Next FOMC meeting Jan 27-28 expected to hold steady (confirmed: held). Two dissenting members (Miran, Waller) preferred another 25bp cut. 10-year Treasury yield around 4.1-4.2%. Gold rallied 9% in January on geopolitical uncertainty, GLD went from $421.29 (Jan 16) to $437.23 (Jan 20) to $443.60 (Jan 21). WTI crude below $60, weak. IMF raised China 2026 growth forecast to 4.5% on US trade truce. Chief Economists at Davos discussed AI productivity boost of 0.1-0.8% to global GDP.

sections.title: Corporate
sections.content: KEY EARNINGS JAN 21: Johnson & Johnson reported Q4 before market open - beat with $2.46 adj EPS, revenue $24.6B (+9.1%). 2026 guidance above consensus at $99.5-100.5B revenue. Stock relatively flat at $218.21 (from $218.66). Netflix reported Jan 20 after close - beat EPS ($0.56 vs $0.55) and revenue ($12.05B vs $11.97B), 325M subscribers, but 2026 guidance disappointed (11-13% growth slowdown). NFLX dropped from $87.26 to $85.36 (-2.2%). 3M reported Jan 20 - beat EPS $1.83 vs $1.81, but stock dropped hard from $167.80 to $155.88 (-7.1%) on Jan 21. Ericsson reported strong Q4 with 6% organic growth and SEK 25B shareholder distribution plan, stock surged ~11%. Procter & Gamble earnings due Jan 22 (beat). Intel earnings due Jan 22 after close.

sections.title: TechAI
sections.content: AI infrastructure spending remains the dominant investment theme. Nvidia has $275B backlog, expected $65B Q4 revenue. Chinese companies ordered 2M+ H200 chips potentially worth $40B. AMD surged 7.7% on Jan 21 ($231.83 to $249.80) on Turin server CPU demand - nearly sold out for 2026, potential 15% price hikes. Bernstein upgraded AMD server forecast to 30% growth. Intel surged 11% ($48.56 to $54.25) on server CPU demand + upcoming earnings. Davos attendees expressed concerns about AI bubble but acknowledged 0.1-0.8% GDP boost potential. Broadcom fell from $351.71 to $332.60 on Jan 21 despite broad market rally - unusual weakness.

sections.title: Energy
sections.content: WTI crude below $60, testing resistance near $62. Kazakhstan halted Tengiz/Korolev oil production temporarily due to power issues. Trump at Davos highlighted US natural gas production at all-time highs, oil production up 730K bpd. XLE flat ($47.69 to $47.60 on Jan 21). Energy is not a catalyst here - sidelined by low prices and oversupply narrative. Trump executive order banning large institutional investors from buying single-family homes was a Davos announcement.

sections.title: Policy
sections.content: Trump's Davos speech covered: (1) Greenland framework deal/tariff pause - biggest market mover. (2) 'Won't use force' for Greenland - de-escalation. (3) Executive order banning institutional investors from buying single-family homes. (4) Claims of 1.6% core inflation and 5.4% Q4 GDP growth. (5) Iran tariff threats: 25% on any country doing business with Iran, 'effective immediately.' Supreme Court IEEPA tariff case pending - would ultimately rule tariffs unconstitutional on Feb 20. NATO Golden Dome missile defense initiative projected at $1.1T.

scenarios.trade: AMD demonstrated remarkable relative strength by holding $231.83 through the Jan 20 selloff while the S&P dropped 2.1%. The Turin CPU demand catalyst is company-specific and powerful - being sold out for a full year with pricing power is rare. The tariff relief rally provides a macro tailwind on top of the fundamental catalyst. This is a convergence trade: strong idiosyncratic catalyst + macro relief + technical resilience.

scenarios.implication: Broader market could continue declining if tariff relief doesn't materialize as expected. AI spending fears from Davos bubble concerns. Intel earnings on Jan 22 could steal thunder if very strong. Risk of rotation away from semis after recent outperformance.

scenarios.trade: Intel is in the midst of a multi-catalyst setup: server CPU demand sold out (matching AMD narrative), analyst upgrades, pre-earnings momentum, and the broader tariff relief rally. The stock has been re-rated from turnaround story to growth story. The 140% gain in the past year shows strong institutional momentum. Pre-earnings runs into strong results can be powerful.

scenarios.implication: Earnings on Jan 22 could disappoint and reverse the entire move. At $48.56, the stock has already run significantly - buying the pre-earnings pop is chasing. If earnings miss, the reversal could be severe. Foundry business still unproven at scale. Intel historically disappoints on guidance.

scenarios.trade: This is the highest-probability trade on the board. The Jan 20 selloff was driven by a specific, identifiable geopolitical catalyst (Greenland tariffs) that gets resolved on Jan 21. The Baird report noted investor positioning was extremely bullish going into the selloff, meaning the selloff was more about positioning unwind than fundamental deterioration. Once the tariff threat is removed, the dip-buyers return aggressively. The S&P was only 2.6% from all-time highs.

scenarios.implication: The tariff pause could be seen as temporary (framework not a deal). Morning of Jan 21 markets were 'still sinking' - if Trump's Davos speech disappoints, the selloff deepens. Supreme Court IEEPA case creates lingering tariff uncertainty. Positioning was overcrowded bullish per Baird.

scenarios.trade: Netflix is a rare short opportunity on a broadly bullish day. When a stock can't rally with the market after reporting earnings, it signals that sellers are in control. The 2026 guidance showing 11-13% growth is a meaningful deceleration that re-rates the multiple lower. The stock declining while the Dow surges 580 points is a powerful negative divergence. Fund managers who were overweight will need to reduce positions.

scenarios.implication: Broad market rally could eventually lift all boats including NFLX. 325M subscribers and 150% ad revenue growth are genuinely impressive. Short squeezes in beaten-down names on risk-on days. Stop is tight - need quick execution.

scenarios.trade: Tesla is a high-beta play on the tariff relief rally. The stock dropped more than the broader market on Jan 20, creating room for an outsized bounce. European tariff removal is directly relevant given Tesla's significant European manufacturing (Giga Berlin) and sales exposure. Tesla trades as a sentiment/momentum vehicle, and the shift from fear to relief is its optimal environment.

scenarios.implication: Tesla's fundamental valuation remains stretched. Musk's political activities create headline risk. European competition from VW/BYD intensifying. If the market rally fizzles, high-beta names get hit hardest. Auto tariff risks remain beyond Greenland.

scenarios.trade: 3M is the clearest short setup: stock crashes on a massively positive tape day. The earnings 'beat' was marginal (2 cents) and the forward guidance, while solid, doesn't justify the turnaround premium the stock had built up. Institutional holders are using the results as a distribution opportunity. The -7.1% move on a +1.2% market day is among the worst relative performances, signaling more selling ahead.

scenarios.implication: The magnitude of the Jan 21 drop may already price in the negative reaction - could bounce on Jan 22. 3M's turnaround fundamentals (margin expansion, product launches) are genuine. Could catch a short squeeze if the broad market continues rallying. Entry at Jan 20 close means you ride the full gap down.

watchlist.name: Broadcom
watchlist.note: Fell $19 (5.4%) on Jan 21 despite broad market rally and semi peers surging. Unusual weakness warrants watching for breakdown continuation, but unclear catalyst makes it a watch not a trade.

watchlist.name: iShares MSCI Germany ETF
watchlist.note: Direct tariff relief beneficiary but European ETFs traded on US exchanges show muted reaction on Jan 21 ($42.54 to $42.82, +0.7%) because European markets already closed when tariff pause announced. The real move comes Jan 22. Watch for entry.

watchlist.name: SPDR Gold Shares
watchlist.note: Gold rallying 9% in January. GLD from $437.23 to $443.60 on Jan 21 (+1.5%). Momentum strong but unclear if tariff de-escalation reduces safe-haven demand. Better as a multi-day hold than day trade.

watchlist.name: Ericsson
watchlist.note: Surged ~11% on strong Q4 earnings and SEK 25B shareholder distribution. However, lower liquidity for US-listed ADRs makes day-trading risky. Watch for continuation.

watchlist.name: Johnson & Johnson
watchlist.note: Strong earnings with above-consensus 2026 guidance ($99.5-100.5B revenue). Stock flat at $218.21 - defensive name not benefiting from risk-on rotation. Could be a laggard that catches up later.

avoidList.name: Energy Select Sector SPDR
avoidList.reason: WTI below $60, flat XLE, Trump touting record US production. No catalyst for energy day-trades. Avoid.

avoidList.name: Utilities Select Sector SPDR
avoidList.reason: Risk-on day means rotation out of defensive/yield sectors. Utilities will underperform.

avoidList.name: SPDR Euro Stoxx 50 ETF
avoidList.reason: Despite being a tariff relief beneficiary, FEZ actually declined on Jan 21 ($66.59 to $66.00) because the tariff pause came after European markets closed. The US-listed ETF reacted to morning European weakness, not the afternoon relief. Timing mismatch makes this a trap.
